dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:3501.text: White 棣. Formed from 木, with 隶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3502.text: A tree resembling the mandarin orange. Formed from 木, with 只 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3503.text: A tree with thick leaves and supple branches, readily swaying; also called 欇. Formed from 木, with 風 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3504.text: A yellow-flowered tree. Formed from 木, with 雚 indicating the sound. Another explanation: contrary to the usual.

shuowen:3505.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 巨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3506.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 鬼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3507.text: The 楮 tree. Formed from 木, with 㱿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3508.text: The 榖 tree. Formed from 木, with 者 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3509.text: The 枸杞 plant. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 繼 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the 監 tree.

shuowen:3510.text: The 枸杞 plant. Formed from 木, with 己 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3511.text: A kind of palm-like tree whose fruits hang at the top; another sense refers to the joining of the curved wooden rim of a chariot wheel. Formed from 木, with 牙 indicating the sound. [Precise historical botanical identification is not certain.]

shuowen:3512.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 亶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3513.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 樂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3514.text: The clustered or cup-like seed casing of certain trees, traditionally described as the fruit of 櫟. Another explanation: the wooden head or handle of a boring implement. Formed from 木, with 求 indicating the sound. [The botanical and tool identifications vary among commentaries.]

shuowen:3515.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 柬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3516.text: Mountain mulberry. Formed from 木, with 厭 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Those 檿 and those 柘 trees.”

shuowen:3517.text: A mulberry. Formed from 木, with 石 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3518.text: A tree used for staffs. Formed from 木, with 厀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3519.text: 𣟳味, a ripe jujube. Formed from 木, with 還 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3520.text: The 梧桐 tree, also called 櫬. Formed from 木, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3521.text: The 桐 tree. Formed from 木, with abbreviated 熒 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the raised ends of a building’s eaves are called 榮.

shuowen:3522.text: The 榮 tree. Formed from 木, with 同 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3523.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 番 indicating the sound. Read like 樊.

shuowen:3524.text: 榆 is the white 枌 elm. Formed from 木, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3525.text: An elm. Formed from 木, with 分 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3526.text: A spiny variety of mountain elm whose seed pods can be processed to make 蕪夷, a traditional aromatic medicinal preparation. Formed from 木, with 更 indicating the sound. [Commentaries differ over the exact elm species.]

shuowen:3527.text: Scattered wood. Formed from 木, with 焦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3528.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 公 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3529.text: Pine heartwood. Formed from 木, with 㒼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3530.text: A tree with cypress leaves and a pine trunk. Formed from 木, with 會 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3531.text: A tree with pine leaves and a cypress trunk. Formed from 木, with 從 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3532.text: The 鞠 tree. Formed from 木, with 白 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3533.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 几 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3534.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 占 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3535.text: A tree. Formed from 木, with 弄 indicating the sound. Yizhou has Longdong County, 梇棟.

shuowen:3536.text: The 鼠梓 tree. Formed from 木, with 臾 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “On the northern mountain grow 楰.”

shuowen:3537.text: A yellow tree usable as dye. Formed from 木, with 危 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3538.text: 桎杒, a kind of tree. Formed from 木, with 刃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3539.text: 榙𣝋, a tree. Formed from 木, with 遝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3540.text: 榙𣝋, with plum-like fruit. Formed from 木, with 荅 indicating the sound. Read like 嚃.

shuowen:3541.text: A sour fruit. Formed from 木 and 甘. Further explanation is missing.

shuowen:3542.text: A tall tree at a bend of the Kunlun River. Formed from 木, with 繇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3543.text: A general name for growing plants. Formed from 木, with 尌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3544.text: The lower part of a tree is called 本. Formed from 木, with 一 beneath it.

shuowen:3545.text: Tree roots. Formed from 木, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3546.text: A red-hearted tree of the pine and cypress kind. Formed from 木, with 一 in its middle.

shuowen:3547.text: A tree stump or rootstock. Formed from 木, with 艮 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3548.text: Tree roots. Formed from 木, with 朱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3549.text: The upper part of a tree is called 末. Formed from 木, with 一 above it.

shuowen:3550.text: Fine-grained wood. Formed from 木, with 畟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3551.text: Tree fruit. Formed from 木, depicting fruit above the tree.

shuowen:3552.text: Tree fruit. Formed from 木, with 絫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3553.text: A branch. Formed from 木, with 叉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3554.text: A shoot growing separately from a tree. Formed from 木, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3555.text: Tree bark. Formed from 木, with 卜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3556.text: A small branch. Formed from 木, with 攸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3557.text: A stem, usable as a staff. Formed from 木 and 攴. The Odes says: “Extending to the branches and stems.”

shuowen:3558.text: To notch as a marker. Formed from 木 and 纨; further explanation is missing. The Book of Xia says: “Following the mountains, marking the trees.” Read like 刊.

shuowen:3559.text: Tree leaves swaying and showing white. Formed from 木, with 聶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3560.text: A weak appearance. Formed from 木, with 任 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3561.text: The young and flourishing appearance of a tree. Formed from 木, with 夭 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “The peach tree is young and flourishing.”

shuowen:3562.text: The top of a tree. Formed from 木, with 眞 indicating the sound. Another explanation: a fallen tree.

shuowen:3563.text: A single stem or piece. Formed from 木, with 廷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3564.text: Numerous and flourishing. Formed from 木, with 驫 indicating the sound. In a quotation from the Lost Documents of Zhou, the graph may refer to accumulating doubts that impede affairs. [Duan regards the final 闕 as a later addition and disputes parts of the transmitted quotation.]

shuowen:3565.text: The tip of a tree. Formed from 木, with 𤐫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3566.text: The tip of a tree. Formed from 木, with 少 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3567.text: Trees drooping, 朵朵. Formed from 木; pictographic. This uses the same principle as 𥝩.

shuowen:3568.text: A tall tree. Formed from 木, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3569.text: The appearance of a large tree. Formed from 木, with 閒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3570.text: A tree root. Formed from 木, with 号 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The year-star is in 玄枵.” 玄枵 means empty.

shuowen:3571.text: A tree’s swaying appearance. Formed from 木, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3572.text: A tree moving. Formed from 木, with 䍃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3573.text: Bending downward is called 樛. Formed from 木, with 翏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3574.text: A tall tree. Formed from 木, with 丩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3575.text: Crooked or bent. Formed from 木, with 㞷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3576.text: Bent wood. Formed from 木, with 堯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3577.text: 枎疏: spreading in all directions. Formed from 木, with 夫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3578.text: A tree spreading, 檹施. Formed from 木, with 旖 indicating the sound. Palace Attendant Jia says 檹 is the 椅 tree, usable for making zithers.

shuowen:3579.text: Rising above one another. Formed from 木, with 小 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3580.text: A lofty appearance. Formed from 木, with 曶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3581.text: The appearance of tall plants. Formed from 木, with 參 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Unevenly grows the floating-heart.”

shuowen:3582.text: Tall timber. Formed from 木, with 延 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Long are the pine rafters.”

shuowen:3583.text: The appearance of tall trees. Formed from 木, with 肅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3584.text: A tree’s appearance. Formed from 木, with 大 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “That solitary 杜 tree.”

shuowen:3585.text: Tree leaves falling. Formed from 木, with 㲋 indicating the sound. Read like 薄.

shuowen:3586.text: The appearance of tall trees. Formed from 木, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3587.text: Wood rubbing against wood. Formed from 木, with 埶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3588.text: Withered. Formed from 木, with 古 indicating the sound. The Book of Xia says: “Only 箘, 輅 and 枯”; there it is a tree name.

shuowen:3589.text: Wood withered. Formed from 木, with 高 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3590.text: Wood in its plain, unworked state. Formed from 木, with 菐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3591.text: Hard timber. Formed from 木, with 貞 indicating the sound. Shang Commandery has Zhenlin County, 楨林.

shuowen:3592.text: Wood that bends and straightens. Formed from 木, with 矛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3593.text: To split. Formed from 木, with 㡿 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Double gates, with clappers struck.”

shuowen:3594.text: The grain of wood. Formed from 木, with 力 indicating the sound. Pingyuan has a county called 朸.

shuowen:3595.text: A stem of wood. Formed from 木, with 才 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3596.text: Small wood and scattered timber. Formed from 木, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3597.text: 榑桑, the divine tree where the sun rises. Formed from 木, with 尃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:3598.text: Bright. Formed from 日 above 木.

shuowen:3599.text: Dark. Formed from 日 below 木.

shuowen:3600.text: A horn-shaped implement. Formed from 木, with 卻 indicating the sound. Another explanation: the white part beneath wood. Both descriptions are uncertain.
